reason: The cited README lines describe browser_fill_form as filling multiple form fields with supplied field values and mark it read-only false. That supports SINK because agent-supplied data can be written into a browser page/form, an attacker-readable destination when the page is controlled by or observable to an attacker. The lines do not show arbitrary host code execution, access to non-public/local data returned into context, or returning attacker-controllable page content. The coreBundle excerpt is for a different toolName (browser_type), not browser_fill_form, and does not add support for those labels.
